28: Request under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 to transfer the case to another court was denied as not in the interest of justice.
We do not believe that transferring Mr. Bowles' case to yet another forum would be in the interest of justice.
322: Forum non conveniens dismissal (venue/transfer ruling): whether the Federal Court of Canada was an adequate alternative forum for the design patent, copyright, and trademark claims. The court held the district court abused its discretion, so dismissal was improper.
Because we hold that the district court abused its discretion and therefore that dismissal on forum non conveniens grounds was improper, we need not address Halo's remaining arguments
340: Transfer under 28 U.S.C. § 1631: the requested transfer in the interest of justice was denied.
We are not persuaded that transferring this case is in the interest of justice.
710: Venue and transfer: the Southern District of Ohio transferred the infringement action to the District of New Jersey under 28 U.S.C. § 1404(a) on the defendants' motion; the Federal Circuit affirmed as no clear abuse of discretion.
On this record, we discern no clear abuse of discretion in the district court's decision to transfer the case to the District of New Jersey.
1009: Denial of Taylor's motion to transfer his district court complaint to the Court of Federal Claims.
we hold that, because the United States Court of Federal Claims would lack jurisdiction over Mr. Taylor’s claims, we must affirm the order denying transfer.
1024: Whether the Court of Federal Claims properly declined to transfer the case to a district court under 28 U.S.C. § 1631, given failure to exhaust and no other waiver of sovereign immunity.
We therefore conclude that transfer of this case to a district court is not warranted.
1068: Whether to transfer the appeal to the Court of Federal Claims under 28 U.S.C. § 1631. The court declined transfer because it was not in the interest of justice, given the untimeliness of the claim there.

At a minimum, it does not seem to us to be in the interest of justice to transfer this matter, given all the facts, once we decide, as we have, that we lack jurisdiction to review the Board's decision.
1237: Request to transfer the case back to the San Jose Division within the Northern District of California was rejected as a proper intra-district venue decision.
San Jose and San Francisco are both in the Northern District of California; the decision to change venue within the district was entirely proper.
1252: Denial of Brown's motion to transfer the case to a district court under the interest-of-justice standard; affirmed.
We conclude that the Court of Federal Claims properly denied Mr. Brown's motion to transfer.
1339: Venue and transfer: Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion in declining to transfer the case to district court under 28 U.S.C. 1631.
The Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion in deciding not to transfer Mr. Robleto's case to a district court.
1677: Refusal to transfer the FTCA case to district court under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because the plaintiff failed to administratively exhaust the claim; no abuse of discretion.

The Claims Court correctly determined that it should not transfer the case because Ms. Canuto failed to satisfy the jurisdictional requirement of exhausting her FTCA claim with the administrative agency prior to filing suit.
1688: Request that the second complaint be transferred to the GAO or DOJ rather than dismissed. Denied, and affirmed.
Wright offers no legal authority for this requested transfer, much less for the GAO or DOJ to adjudicate his claims in the first place.
1769: Declining to transfer the case under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because no federal court would have jurisdiction under the Rooker-Feldman doctrine.
Therefore, the Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion in declining to transfer Mr. Betts's case under 28 U.S.C. § 1631.
2012: Transfer under 28 U.S.C. § 1631: the Claims Court declined to transfer the case because it was not in the interest of justice given the failure to state a claim.
The Claims Court also did not err by declining to transfer the case pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1631.
2327: Biogen's request that the Federal Circuit retransfer the case to the district court was denied.
We therefore decline to transfer this case back to the district court.
2530: Denial of transfer of the FTCA claim to district court under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because no district court would have had jurisdiction, given failure to file an administrative claim with the agency.

We agree with the Claims Court that no district court would have possessed jurisdiction over Mr. Montano's FTCA claim at the time he filed it in the Claims Court and, therefore, affirm the Claims Court's decision that it could not transfer Mr. Montano's case.
2694: Belated motion by Mr. Allen to transfer the appeal to the District Court for the District of Columbia was denied.
We, therefore, deny Mr. Allen's request to transfer his appeal.
3631: Venue and transfer: whether the CIT could transfer the action to the D.C. District Court on remand; court held the transfer request was implicitly foreclosed by the mandate in Best Key I because the CIT has exclusive jurisdiction under 1581(a).
Because the CIT would possess exclusive jurisdiction over any such denied protest, the CIT did not err in finding Best Key's transfer request implicitly foreclosed by Best Key I.
3906: Denial of Khan's request to transfer the case to S.D.N.Y. under 28 U.S.C. 1631 as not in the interest of justice.
The Claims Court also properly rejected Ms. Khan's request to transfer the case to S.D.N.Y.
3978: Venue: denial of TTI's motion to transfer venue after TC Heartland as untimely and forfeited, affirmed as no abuse of discretion.
The district court did not abuse its discretion in denying TTI's motion to transfer venue under the circumstances here.
4206: Denial of transfer under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 to a federal court with jurisdiction; the court held the plaintiff failed to identify a transferee court where jurisdiction would be proper, so dismissal without transfer was appropriate.
Because Mr. Maehr failed to show jurisdiction would be proper in another court, the Court of Federal Claims could not transfer the case.
4352: Venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1400(b) was improper for the defendants; dismissal for improper venue affirmed.
The district court correctly concluded that venue was improper under § 1400(b).
4488: Whether the Claims Court was required to transfer the case under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 instead of dismissing
We agree with the government that 28 U.S.C. § 1631 did not require the Claims Court to transfer this case.
4954: Venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1400(b): the district court properly dismissed for improper venue because the plaintiff failed to plead facts showing a regular and established place of business in the district.
we hold the district court did not err in granting 3M's motion to dismiss.
4967: Whether the Court of Federal Claims abused its discretion in refusing to transfer the case under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 to the district court or the Veterans Court.
The Court of Federal Claims also correctly concluded that it could not transfer Mr. Vincent's claim to the Veterans Court because the [Veterans Court] is not a 'court' within the meaning of § 1631.
4977: Claims Court did not abuse its discretion in declining to transfer the case to district court under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because the record did not establish presentment, so the transferee court's jurisdiction was not shown.
We also conclude that the Claims Court did not abuse its discretion in deciding not to transfer the case to a district court.
5126: Government's motion to sever the overpayment interest claims over $10,000 and transfer them to the Court of Federal Claims (denied by the district court); the Federal Circuit held the claims must be severed and transferred.
Rather, the Court of Federal Claims has exclusive jurisdiction over those claims, see 28 U.S.C. § 1491(a)(1), and therefore, those claims must be severed and transferred.
5191: Venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1391(d) in the Northern District of Texas; court held venue proper and reversed the dismissal for improper venue.
We conclude that PET is subject to personal jurisdiction in the Northern District of Texas, and that venue is proper in the Northern District.
5410: Court declined to transfer the appeal under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because transfer was not in the interest of justice given the frivolous claims.
We conclude that transfer is not in the interest of justice since Polidi's claims are frivolous.
5542: Transfer of the case from the District of Oregon to the Southern District of California under the venue statute after TC Heartland; transfer upheld.
we do not find that the district court needs to retransfer this case back to Oregon.
6184: Venue and transfer: the district court's transfer of the patent case from the Western District of Texas to the District of Delaware under 28 U.S.C. § 1406 for improper venue under § 1400(b) was affirmed.
We thus conclude that UT does not have the right to bring a patent infringement suit against BSC in the Western District of Texas, an improper venue.
6418: Dismissal of the first-filed declaratory judgment action under the first-to-file rule and the Declaratory Judgment Act in favor of Contec's later-filed New York infringement action; the court affirmed the dismissal as a proper exercise of discretion, including on convenience-of-forum grounds.
The district court dismissed CTDI’s declaratory judgment action so that Contec’s patent infringement action—filed six days later—could proceed in New York.
6454: Whether the Claims Court must consider transfer of the NAHASDA claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1631; the court held the Claims Court should consider transfer in the first instance and rejected the government's argument that transfer was foreclosed.
We conclude that on the record before us, the Claims Court should consider in the first instance whether to transfer Lummi's NAHASDA claim pursuant to § 1631.
7045: Venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1400(b) for Hatch-Waxman ANDA infringement claims against domestic Mylan defendants (MPI and Mylan Inc.); dismissal for improper venue affirmed.

we hold that venue in Hatch-Waxman cases must be predicated on past acts of infringement—i.e., acts that occurred before the action alleging infringement was filed. And we hold those acts occur only in districts where actions related to the ANDA submission occur.
7331: Denial of Huang's motion to transfer venue from the Eastern District of Texas to the Northern District of California under 28 U.S.C. § 1404; no abuse of discretion found.
we do not find an abuse of discretion in the district court's denial of Mr. Huang's motion.
7488: Venue and transfer: whether the district court properly transferred the Equal Pay Act claim to the Court of Federal Claims under 28 U.S.C. § 1631; the transfer order was affirmed.
And, having been presented no other valid reason to disturb that order, we affirm it.
8074: Venue under 28 U.S.C. 1400(b) as to Cargill, a third-party counterclaim defendant; court affirmed denial of Cargill's motion to dismiss for improper venue.
we affirm the district court's determination that venue as to Cargill was proper in the Eastern District of Virginia.
8495: Whether the district court properly transferred the EPA claim to the Court of Federal Claims under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 rather than dismissing it; transfer affirmed.
For the foregoing reasons, and because we see no other impediment to the Court of Federal Claims' jurisdiction over Dr. Metzinger's EPA claim, we affirm the district court's transfer to that court.
8993: Transfer of the action under 28 U.S.C. §1404(a) from N.D. Cal. to E.D. Tex.; Mitek's challenge to transfer order rejected
In any event, Mitek has not demonstrated an abuse of discretion—e.g., legal error, unreasonableness, clear factual error—in the transfer order issued by the California district court.
9131: Dismissal of Arendi II complaint as duplicative of Arendi I (duplicative-litigation doctrine), a procedural case-management ruling reviewed for abuse of discretion
we affirm the district court's dismissal of the complaint.
9826: Venue and transfer: Parks' motion to transfer to the Central District of California was denied and affirmed.
We also see no basis for transferring this case.
10862: Venue under 28 U.S.C. § 1400(b): the court held that submitting the ANDA was the only infringing act and that the paragraph IV notice letter received in New Jersey did not make the defendants' acts there infringing, so venue was improper for MPI and Mylan Inc.
Accordingly, we conclude that Celgene did not establish that the defendants-appellees committed an act of infringement in New Jersey.
10863: Venue under § 1400(b): the court held that the homes, storage lockers, and the defunct subsidiary's New Jersey office were not regular and established places of business of MPI or Mylan Inc., and declined to impute them to those defendants.
In summary, the employee-associated locations are not a regular and established place of business of the defendants under § 1400(b).
11847: Transfer: denial of transfer under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because no other court had jurisdiction over bid protests
there was no court to which the Court of Federal Claims could transfer Ms. Monbo’s case.
12736: Venue and transfer: the district court's denial of transfer under §1404(a) and its finding that venue was proper in the Western District of Michigan were not disturbed; the court found no clear and indisputable right to mandamus.

And the district court reasonably weighed the relevant factors under § 1404(a) and considered Mr. Surti's arguments before concluding that transfer to the Middle District of Tennessee was unjustified.
13105: Transfer of the case from the Southern District of New York to the Eastern District of North Carolina on Teleflex's venue objection
Accordingly, the district court did not abuse its discretion in transferring this case from the Southern District of New York to the Eastern District of North Carolina.
13171: May's request to transfer the appeal to a federal court in New York was denied.
13255: Venue and transfer: the court transferred the appeal to the United States District Court for the District of Columbia under 28 U.S.C. 1631, at Jones's suggestion, over the Board's silence on transfer.
In these circumstances, we transfer the present appeal to the district court for the District of Columbia under 28 U.S.C. § 1631.
13588: Claims Court's transfer of the case to the Eastern District of Virginia under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 was proper and not an abuse of discretion.
We also agree that the Claims Court properly transferred this case to the United States District Court of the Eastern District of Virginia.
13647: Motion to transfer the petition to the District of Nebraska denied as underdeveloped and abandoned
We find Mr. Dowling's argument to be underdeveloped and therefore abandoned.
13909: Denial of transfer to district court because the claim seeks money and the district court lacks jurisdiction over it.
The Claims Court did not abuse its discretion by declining to transfer his case.
13985: Denial of the claimant's request to transfer the case to the Northern District of Illinois under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 because transfer was not in the interest of justice; the court found no abuse of discretion.
The Claims Court did not abuse its discretion by declining to transfer Mr. Boultbee's case.
14351: Denial of motion to disqualify Judge Tapp under 28 U.S.C. §455 (recusal), with assignment under RCFC 40.2 upheld.
We thus affirm the Claims Court's denial of Dr. Aljindi's recusal motion.
14415: Venue and transfer: request to transfer the case to a district court under 28 U.S.C. § 1631 was denied; no abuse of discretion.
The Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion in not transferring this case given that Ms. Stevenson first requested transfer on appeal to this Court.
14637: Transfer: the court declined Montanez's request to transfer the petition to federal district court under 28 U.S.C. 1631 as not in the interest of justice.
We decline to transfer this case because transfer is not in the interest of justice under 28 U.S.C. § 1631.
15050: Denial of motion to transfer venue under 28 U.S.C. 1400(b) after TC Heartland, based on forfeiture of venue objection; affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the district court's denial of Appellants' motion to dismiss or transfer venue.
